title: Leader in adult care
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Leading the care service and managing teams of carers to look after adults with care needs.

knowledges.detail: Leadership and management approaches to support team performance and delivery of organisational objectives.
Ethical leadership approaches and decision‑making in practice.
Techniques for promoting positive organisational culture and inclusive and psychologically safe environments, and the impact of communicating visions and values on engagement and accountability.
Workforce development approaches, including Continuous Professional Development, coaching, mentoring, and learning cultures, to maintain competence and capability.
Workforce planning, monitoring, and staffing models to maintain service quality.
Recruitment approaches aligned with workforce needs and policy requirements.
Approaches to supervision, appraisal and performance management.
Person‑centred approaches, including strengths‑based and co‑produced care.
Advocacy approaches and the influence of organisational culture on outcomes.
Approaches to monitoring and evaluating trauma‑informed care and Positive Behaviour Support.
Stakeholder roles, responsibilities, and collaborative working across integrated health and social care systems.
Safeguarding frameworks and their implications for accountability and governance.
The role of services within safeguarding enquiries and investigations.
Health and safety requirements, incident reporting, and safe systems of work.
Risk assessment approaches to identify and respond to hazards.
Financial planning, compliance, and performance monitoring systems.
Approaches to procurement and sustainable resource management, including consideration of environmental, social and economic factors.
National policy for monitoring record‑keeping, reporting, maintaining confidentiality and information security.
Models and approaches for planning and implementing organisational change.
Leadership communication styles and how to adapt these to motivate and support stakeholders.
Approaches to quality assurance models that drive evidence-based improvements and outcomes.

skills.detail: Apply leadership and management approaches to lead teams and deliver organisational objectives.
Apply ethical leadership approaches to support decision‑making and professional practice.
Promote inclusive and psychologically safe environments and communicate vision and values to support engagement and accountability.
Manage workforce development through Continuous Professional Development, coaching, and mentoring to maintain competence and capability.
Apply workforce planning and staffing models to maintain service quality.
Apply recruitment approaches to attract and select individuals aligned to organisational values and workforce needs.
Apply processes to review performance, address issues and support continuous improvement.
Apply strengths‑based and co‑produced approaches to lead and advise teams to deliver personalised care.
Promote and apply advocacy approaches to improve outcomes.
Monitor and evaluate the use of trauma-informed care and Positive Behaviour Support in line with frameworks.
Work with stakeholders to support integrated care and coordinated outcomes.
Apply safeguarding frameworks to ensure safe and accountable practice.
Contribute to safeguarding enquiries and investigations as a stakeholder.
Implement health and safety procedures and safe systems of work.
Apply risk assessment to manage risks.
Apply financial and performance monitoring approaches to support compliance and service delivery.
Apply procurement and sustainable resource management approaches, including consideration of environmental, social and economic factors.
Apply monitoring processes to ensure accurate records and maintain information security and confidentiality.
Apply change management approaches to plan and implement organisational change.
Adapt communication approaches to engage, motivate and support stakeholders.
Plans and implements quality assurance models to drive evidence-based improvements and outcomes.

duties.dutyDetail: Lead workforce recruitment, development and performance management to build a resilient, skilled and future ready workforce.
Motivate and engage team members to collaborate towards shared goals, fostering an inclusive culture that supports learning, mentoring, and continuous professional development.
Champion personalised, strengths‑based and co‑produced care, ensuring all voices, rights and aspirations shape all support and decision‑making.
Ensure robust health and safety practices through dynamic risk management, consistent incident reporting, and proactive mitigation of hazards.
Lead and oversee safeguarding policies and procedures for adults, that comply with local and national legislation.
Evaluate and apply organisational contingency plans to maintain continuity of care during critical incidents or service disruptions.
Build strong, collaborative partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to champion high‑quality social care and deliver better outcomes across the wider care and health system.
Set and communicate a clear strategic vision that aligns team purpose, strengthens service direction and ensures everyone understands their contribution to shared goals.
Lead effective financial planning, budget management and resource allocation to ensure operational sustainability and alignment with strategic priorities.
Embed sustainable and environmentally responsible practices across service delivery, resource planning and organisational culture.
Promote a compassionate, equitable and inclusive culture that values diversity and enhances the wellbeing of people drawing on care, staff and wider communities.
Drive organisational change using recognised models and engagement strategies, preparing and influencing stakeholders through transitions and improvements.
Take  responsibility  for continuous personal and professional development through self‑reflection, feedback and evidence informed learning to strengthen leadership and improve outcomes.
Critically apply leadership, management and adult care theories to inform sound decision‑making and enhance service effectiveness.
Ensure full regulatory compliance through strong governance systems, quality assurance processes, accurate documentation, and active preparation for inspections and audits.
